statement: q(tau_Xn omega)=P_0(A_l|F_n) converges a.s. and in L1 to 1_A_l.
assumptions: F_n includes the entire environment and the first n steps
proof: Markov property and finite-prefix invariance give the conditional expectation; Levy upward theorem identifies the limit.
remaining_gap: Independent mathematical check; no finite-region measurability is assumed.

proof: Zeros of q or 1-q propagate along every positive-probability edge; translation ergodicity and their nonzero expectations exclude either zero set having full measure.
remaining_gap: Positivity is not the target zero-one law.

statement: Law(tau_Xn omega) has P-density f_n=sum_{|x|_1<=n}P_{-x}^omega(X_n=0), with E_P f_n=1.
proof: Finite endpoint decomposition, change variable omega'=tau_x omega, and translation covariance of quenched paths.
remaining_gap: Finite-time density is not a stationary environment law or a uniform integrability bound.

statement: Mixed directional transience forces E_P f_n^r->infinity for every r>1 and excludes every uniformly integrable time-diverging subsequence of f_n or its Cesaro averages.
assumptions: stationary ergodic strict-elliptic static nearest-neighbor RWRE
proof: B_epsilon={q<=epsilon or q>=1-epsilon} has P-mass tending to zero and mu_n-mass tending to one. Holder gives E f_n^r >= mu_n(B_epsilon)^r/P(B_epsilon)^(r-1); uniform absolute continuity contradicts concentration, also after Cesaro averaging.
remaining_gap: No bounded-moment or uniform integrability estimate follows from the current target hypotheses.

statement: Subsequential uniform integrability of incoming environment densities f_n, or their Cesaro averages, implies the directional zero-one law.
assumptions: stationary ergodic strict-elliptic static nearest-neighbor RWRE
deterministic unbounded time subsequence with uniformly integrable incoming densities or Cesaro densities
proof: Assume mixed probability; Lemma 4 contradicts the additional uniform integrability hypothesis.
remaining_gap: Prove the extra density assumption from C0044 assumptions. This is not a solution of C0044.

statement: Normalization and individual absolute continuity do not imply uniform integrability.
counterexample: Each g_m has integral one, while for m>K its entire mass is above K and its r-moment is m^(r-1).
remaining_gap: This family is not claimed to arise from iid RWRE.
